title: Exfoliating foot cream
subtitle: A thick cream with pumice for rough heels and callused soles
excerpt: Foot cream with pumice is a thick, gritty cream made from shea butter, coconut oil, and pumice powder, formulated for rough heels and callused soles. It exfoliates on application and leaves a protective, conditioning film as it absorbs. Makes about 100 g in a small jar; keeps six months in a cool cupboard.
sourceNotes: Shea butter and coconut oil as a base for foot cream: The Handmade Apothecary by Kim Walker and Vicky Chown (2017, Kyle Books). Pumice as a cosmetic exfoliant: International Nomenclature of Cosmetic Ingredients (INCI) entry: Pumice (volcanic ash, insoluble mineral). Urea in foot care formulations: Cosmetic Ingredient Review published monograph (2010). Tea tree essential oil for foot hygiene: Australian Tea Tree Industry Association technical notes (2021).

recipe.batchNotes: Double the recipe and fill two jars.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Allow the cream to cool and set before sealing. The pumice settles slightly on standing, stir before use.
recipe.shelfLifeNotes: Six months in a cool cupboard. This is an anhydrous formula (no water), so no preservative is needed. Discard if the cream smells rancid or the oil separates and doesn't re-blend on stirring.

glossaryTerms.definition: A cosmetic formula that contains no water. Anhydrous products do not need a preservative because bacteria and mould require water to grow. Foot creams, balms, and body butters are typically anhydrous.

items.prepNote: refined shea for a neutral scent; unrefined for a nutty base
fine-ground cosmetic-grade pumice; coarse grades are too abrasive for daily use
optional; adds a fresh, clean scent and is traditional in foot-care formulas

content.text: Melt the shea butter and coconut oil together in a heatproof bowl over a pan of simmering water. Remove from heat. Leave to cool until the mixture is semi-solid and opaque, about 30 to 40 minutes at room temperature, or 15 minutes in the fridge. Add the pumice powder and stir through thoroughly. Add the essential oil if using. Spoon into a small jar and leave to set fully before sealing.

Apply a small amount to damp feet and work in circular motions on the heels and ball of the foot where the skin is thickest. Rinse well or wipe off with a warm damp towel. The pumice exfoliates while the oils absorb. Stir the jar before each use as the pumice settles.
Six months in a cool, dry cupboard. Use a dry spoon or spatula to scoop, water in the jar encourages rancidity. Discard if the cream smells sharp or the oil turns yellow and separates.
